newsitem.title: USA: ANALYSIS - U.S. industrial production stays strong.
newsitem.headline: ANALYSIS - U.S. industrial production stays strong.

text.p: Industrial production and capacity utilization figures for February continued to show a healthy U.S. manufacturing sector.

February industrial production rose 0.5 percent following a 0.1 percent drop in January and capacity utilization rose to 83.3 percent from 83.2, much in line with analysts' expectations. Economists had attributed much of the January reading to inclement weather.
"The manufacturing output (up 0.8 percent) was better than expected and industrial output right where we thought it would be," said Sally Kleinman, economist at Chase Securities Inc.
She noted utilities production was down 3.5 percent, but good gains were seen in electrical and industrial machinery as well as aerospace.
Kleinman said the gains represented a widely expected weather rebound.

"I tend to look at manufacturing output and capacity utilization because the industrial production total has utilities in it," said Paul Kasriel, economist at Northern Trust. Both numbers were strong, he added.

"We've bounced back from January and are up from where we were a year ago. There's every reason to expect manufacturing output remains strong as inventories are lean and demand remains strong," Kasriel said.
He predicted further gains in the months ahead.
While growth remains strong, economists said it was not alarmingly so as long as it remained below the 85.0 percent threshold.
As the numbers are tabulated by the Federal Reserve, they provide no surprises to policymakers and are not generally viewed as changing anyone's mind in terms of shifting monetary policy.
